- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if followed by a spike.
- If model shows strong upward momentum after a sharp drop, it often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high if sentiment is neutral or bearish.
- In bearish sentiment (≤0.33), model frequently underestimates downside; add 2–5% buffer to forecast if sentiment is weak or trending down.
- Model often lags in correcting after a strong sentiment reversal; adjust forecast 1–3 days ahead of sentiment shift to avoid delayed mean reversion.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model tends to average out; use sentiment-weighted median of recent 5–7 days to anchor forecast.
- Avoid forecasting sharp reversals unless sentiment is clearly trending; if sentiment is volatile, use 3-day moving average to smooth out noise.
